mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous year's average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 3% over two consecutive months, combined with a concurrent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals a contraction in economic output and demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous year's level by >3% AND RSAFS < previous year's level for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 4% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) alongside a simultaneous rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for three months signals cost-push inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly for three months AND CPIAUCSL > 103 for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, without a concurrent rise in unemployment (UNRATE), suggests forced overtime and labor hoarding, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate future wage growth and margin expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month by >1% AND UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above trend for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when HOUST is above trend for four consecutive months.
